# Pre-launch audit: Ledgerly docs (site type: `docs`) This is a read of the supplied files against the supplied check configuration. I did not run the command or load any page. I applied only the checks whose `applies_to` includes `docs`. ## Established defects **1. No custom 404 page (`custom-error-route`, tier high)** - Affected path: `404.html`, expected at the site root. It is absent site-wide. - Defect: the supplied tree contains only `api.html`, `index.html`, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. There is no `404.html` or `not-found` page. The site does have a static route surface (two HTML pages and a sitemap), so the missing file is a real finding, not a blind spot. - Evidence: the file list has no 404 or not-found page. **2. `api.html` has no meta description (`per-route-metadata`, tier high)** - Affected path: `api.html` - Defect: the `` (lines 3–9) has charset, viewport, title and canonical, but no ``. `index.html` has one, so the omission is specific to this page. - Evidence: `api.html` has no `` anywhere. **3. Duplicate, wrong title across routes (`per-route-metadata`, tier high)** - Affected paths: `api.html` (line 6) and `index.html` (line 6) - Defect: both pages use the identical title `Ledgerly docs — getting started`. The check counts a title shared by more than one page as present but not per-route. On `api.html` the title is also wrong, because the page's `

` is "API reference". - Evidence: `Ledgerly docs — getting started` appears in both files. **4. Image without `alt` (`image-alternative-text`, tier high)** - Affected path: `index.html`, line 12 - Defect: the architecture diagram has no `alt` attribute. It looks like a content image, so it needs descriptive text. If it is purely decorative, it needs an explicit `alt=""`. - Evidence: `` **5. Canonical URL disagrees with the sitemap (`canonical-and-sitemap-coherence`, tier medium)** - Affected paths: `api.html` (line 8), `sitemap.xml` - Defect: the canonical for the API page is on a different host from the one the sitemap and `robots.txt` use. The canonical points at `ledgerly.example`, while the sitemap lists `docs.ledgerly.example`. This sends search engines conflicting signals about the preferred URL. - Evidence: - `api.html`: `` - `sitemap.xml`: `https://docs.ledgerly.example/api` - `index.html` is coherent: its canonical `https://docs.ledgerly.example/` matches its sitemap entry. ## Checks that found nothing in the supplied files - `staging-noindex-leftover`: no noindex meta. `robots.txt` disallows only `/drafts/`, not the whole site. - `https-enforcement` (markup): no `http://` asset URLs. - `document-head-basics`: `lang`, charset and viewport are present on both pages. - `third-party-load-in-markup`, `snippet-eligibility`, `structured-data-parses`: no third-party loads, no `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0`, and no JSON-LD blocks. ## Uncertainties (not counted as defects) - **HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect:** the check's verification step is a `curl` against the live host. That is edge or server configuration, which the supplied files cannot show. - **Hosting-level 404:** the host might serve its own error page. Defect 1 is based on the absence of a 404 file in the supplied build output only. - **Skipped checks:** the legal-page, analytics-consent, superseded-statute, placeholder and privacy-coverage checks do not apply to `docs` and are not findings. No region was declared, so no jurisdictional escalation applies.
